policy.title: Subnational Executive Momentum Reaches 8.3 Net Composite Average Across Fiscal Budgets, Agro-Industrial Parks, and Health Innovations
policy.summary: Nigeria’s state executives record an 8.3 net PSI composite average on October 29, 2026, driven by high-velocity governance across fiscal budget presentations, major land grants for agro-processing, digital health tracking, and offshore energy projections.

policy.introduction:
Subnational executive governance across Nigeria’s 36 States and the Federal Capital Territory recorded strong operational velocity during the active reporting window ending October 29, 2026. The active 16-jurisdiction Policy Signal Index (PSI) baseline settled at a composite average of 8.3, reflecting strong executive commitment to major fiscal budget presentations, maritime shipping expansion, agro-industrial investments, digital health tools, and public sector welfare legislation.

Across the geopolitical zones, state governors and executive councils demonstrated high governance output[cite: 1]. Highlights include Lagos State receiving CMA CGM maritime executives, addressing the NBCC summit, and co-hosting preparations for CANEX 2026; Cross River State presenting a ₦987.8b 2027 budget, expanding soybean farms under Project Grow, and moving to resolve a 20-year communal crisis; Plateau State unveiling plans for a permanent trade fair complex, industrial abattoir, and Agro Rangers harvest protection; Edo State endorsing the OMO-SHINE digital health referral app, launching Orientation Week, and partnering with UBTH; Abia State disbursing relief funds to xenophobia returnees and enforcing Ebola biosecurity; and Delta State assenting to 5 governance bills while granting 99.99 hectares to Olam Agri.
policy.emergingPatterns: The active reporting window reveals a clear focus on agro-industrial scaling, fiscal legislative codification, and public health technology adoption. State governments are systematically pairing capital land grants—such as Delta's 99.99 hectares to Olam Agri—with legislative welfare guarantees like the 13th-Month Salary Law, while leveraging digital tools like Edo's OMO-SHINE app for maternal-child tracking.
policy.strategicOutlook: Sustaining this momentum requires timely legislative passage of presented budgets, rapid execution of agricultural land grants, and continued inter-agency cooperation to protect harvest corridors. States that integrate digital title administration with robust social safety nets will maintain competitive investment advantages.
policy.conclusion: The subnational executive governance landscape for October 29, 2026, demonstrates disciplined policy implementation and institutional growth. By anchoring administrative priorities in capital infrastructure, health biosecurity, and investor confidence, Nigeria's state executives continue to drive economic resilience[cite: 1].

security.introduction: The subnational operational and investment risk climate across Nigeria for October 29, 2026, presents prime opportunities in established commercial, coastal, and industrial hubs, balanced by monitored security frameworks in specific agrarian and border corridors[cite: 1]. Through the B3 State Advisory Data framework, jurisdictions are evaluated using their Policy Signal Index (PSI), raw State Instability Score (SIS), Risk Indicator classification, and derived Investment Decision Profile to guide institutional capital allocation.
security.emergingPatterns: Subnational security mapping confirms that major Southwestern and coastal commercial centers—including Lagos (1.2 SIS), Kwara (1.6 SIS), Oyo (1.7 SIS), Ogun (1.4 SIS), and Cross River (2.0 SIS)—maintain SECURE environments suited for industrial concessions, port operations, and corporate headquarters[cite: 1]. Conversely, Plateau (3.2 SIS) and Zamfara (4.7 SIS) require active risk monitoring, prompting strategic interventions like Plateau's Agro Rangers deployment to protect harvest corridors and Zamfara's fire truck distribution across outer LGAs.
security.strategicOutlook: Institutional investors should leverage high-security coastal corridors for logistics and maritime trade while aligning agribusiness investments in monitored zones with state-supported security frameworks like the Agro Rangers.
security.conclusion: By combining Policy Signal Index ratings with State Instability Scores, corporate planners can navigate subnational markets effectively, identifying high-yield opportunities while maintaining proactive risk management.

jurisdictions.headline: LASWARCO Cracks Down on Illegal Borehole Drilling; DSVA Trains Lawyers on SGBV Prosecution; LASCOPA Resolves 528 IKEDC Complaints

policyBreakdown.category: Environmental Water Regulation, Consumer Protection, and Judicial Reforms

globalCodeData_B3.focus: N63.48bn Executive Assent to State & 27 LGA Supplementary Budgets
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Governor Namadi assented to the N63.48bn Supplementary Budget, allocating N46.37bn for state government infrastructure and N17.11bn across 27 local government councils.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: 86km Road Network Commissioning & 13 LCDA Secretariats Launch
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Commissioned over 86km of rural-urban roads under Network-1100 with Borno Governor Zulum and inaugurated 13 LCDA secretariats including Kwami West.

globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Honoured as FG Best Governor in Education at 2026 World Teachers Day, citing N3.1bn classroom projects and WAEC sponsorships, and approved new Senior Special Assistants and Government House Chief Imam.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: 16-LGA Origin Tech Rural Roads MoU & N2.5bn Social Intervention Cheques
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Presided over 16 LGA MoU signing with Origin Tech for rural roads utilizing N16bn equipment, unveiled Responsible Mining Standards, and presented N2.5bn in social intervention cheques.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: Park Management Law Assent & Federal High Court Asset Freeze Motion
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Signed the Osun Park Management Bill into law, filed Federal High Court motion to vacate an ex-parte asset freeze order obtained by Gamji Nigeria Ltd, and reaffirmed Mrs. Oyebode Mary as Iyaloja General.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: N120m Teachers Merit Awards & Dangote Refinery IPO Share Subscriptions
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Presented N120m in cash prizes to top teachers/schools on World Teachers Day and announced state-funded Dangote Refinery IPO share purchases for active and retired female teachers.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: 6,000MW CLEM Ministerial Retreat & State Treasury Performance Retreat

globalCodeData_B3.focus: 3,000 Basic Education Teachers Recruitment & Ministry Energy Meeting

globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Inspected collapsed East-West Road at Agbarho following 6-day heavy rains, funded Julius Berger palliative works to reopen traffic, and commissioned permanent mini-bridge hydraulic studies.

globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Conducted Independence outreach to Oko Custodial Centre pledging justice review for awaiting-trial inmates, held strike resolution talks with MDCAN, and EDOSEMA distributed flood palliatives in Etsako Central.

globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Disbursed N70.5m in cash rewards to outstanding teachers and school administrators on World Teachers Day, noting over N18bn cumulative executive investment in education.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: N200m Cumulative Victim Relief Support & Kaoje Security Deployment
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Visited Kaoje in Bagudo LGA following security attacks, providing N100m additional support (bringing total state aid to N200m) and deploying additional operational security assets.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: Certificate of Recognition & Staff of Office Presentation to King Jaja VI
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Presented Certificate of Recognition and Staff of Office to King Charles Douglas Mac-Pepple Jaja, Jeki VI as Amanyanabo of Opobo Kingdom, resolving a 27-year chieftaincy legal dispute.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: NNPC OKLNG Project Revival Negotiations & Gateway Port Integration
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Opened discussions with NNPC to revive the Olokola LNG (OKLNG) project on 1,728 hectares, integrating it with the $7bn Gateway Deep Sea Port and Blue Marine Free Zone.

globalCodeData_B3.focus: ESHDC Independence Promo Launch & 10.5km Igogoro-Amaja Road Execution
globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: ESHDC launched Independence property promo offering a free plot grand prize at Smart City Satellite Town, while advancing construction on the 10.5km Igogoro-Ikpamodo-Amaja road corridor.

globalCodeData_B3.dailyBrief: Expanded crop cultivation acreage across rice, maize, and cassava, driving state cassava output past 2.1m metric tonnes and boosting regional food security.
